summary: Weekly Monday sales team meeting run by Chris Klevan with closers Andrew Musial and Richard Claessen and setter Kim Forbes-Sobers. Opens with personal wins, then moves to weekly projections against an $80,000 upfront-cash month target, with Chris pushing Andrew to $50K and pinning Richard to 4 units / $12K for the week. Kim reports zero units set the prior week. The coaching block is aimed at Richard: stop sending payment links and instead collect card details live on the call, never let a prospect go off the call to pay, and how to probe a prospect's finances in discovery without pitching someone who has already signalled they cannot pay. Chris also sets out team roster changes (Harry, Kyla and Ben all gone), a deposit-and-onboarding rule, and his view that the process gets a rep to a 25-40% close rate and the rest is self-development.
notable: Chris Klevan instructs reps not to send payment links and to take card details live instead: 'stop sending payment links' and 'I don't let them get off the phone.' He models overriding a prospect who explicitly asked to pay after the call: 'Well, I can't actually do anything until the payment comes through... I mean, is this something that you actually, like, want to do?'

Chris states a deposit and onboarding rule with figures outside the two-tier offer: 'if you get a $500 deposit, okay, you can book the onboarding call. But they have to pay at least the $1,200 before the onboarding call happens, and if they don't, cancel it.'

A lower-priced product sits in public view at a different price point. Chris: 'if somebody types in Trevor Instinct coaching cost, immediately it says $200 a month. Or if you want one-on-one coaching, it's like somewhere between $400 and $700 a month, which is totally wrong.' Richard asks about moving Primal University to 'that 2k payments on school instead of the 200 a month'.

Chris's stated position on prospects arriving with a wrong price anchor: 'it doesn't really matter if somebody comes in thinking it's a certain price. It's more about just... making sure that you show them the value.'

Kim Forbes-Sobers reports the no-show triage SMS workflow sends its final text from an unassigned company number, so prospects reply asking who is contacting them: 'a lot of the time, that text message will be sent out and people will just respond saying, like, who is this? Because it gets sent from another phone number.'

Roster churn disclosed: Harry Edmonds, Kyla Louie and Ben Byrne are all no longer on the team ('Ben is no longer a part of the team, we mutually talked about it, performance just wasn't there'). Richard Claessen is a new closer, roughly one week in ('Richard, you're obviously, you've been here like a week').
Richard reports collecting $10,000 on the Saturday and that he lost a prospect, Tommy, who went away to talk to his partner and did not come back: 'I know with him also I should have pushed more.'

Chris coaches Richard on qualifying finances in discovery — get clear on whether a prospect genuinely cannot pay before pitching: 'the last thing I want to do is this guy think it's going to be 50 bucks... and I'm going to drop $6,000 on him after I just talk up how great this program is going to be.'
Chris gives a benchmark close rate: 'getting really good at the process, depending on the offer and the marketing of the offer is going to get you anywhere between 25 to 40% close rate.'
The phrase 'Recording has stopped.' appears inline at roughly 00:43:40 while Chris is mid-sentence, though the transcript continues afterwards.
